desc: The Isthmus of Panama is a narrow strip of land connecting North and South America, forming the geographical link between the two continents. It is about 50 km wide at its narrowest point and separates the Caribbean Sea from the Pacific Ocean. The isthmus formed around 3 million years ago, dramatically altering global ocean currents and climate. This event triggered the Great American Interchange, allowing fauna and flora to migrate between North and South America. The Panama Canal, a 82 km artificial waterway completed in 1914, crosses the isthmus, making it one of the most strategically important shipping routes in the world.
fact: The Isthmus of Panama connects North and South America, forming about 3 million years ago · It triggered the Great American Interchange of fauna between the continents · The Panama Canal crosses the isthmus, a vital 82 km global shipping route · The isthmus separated the Atlantic and Pacific, altering global ocean currents and climate

desc: The Isthmus of Suez is a narrow land bridge connecting Africa and Asia, located in eastern Egypt. It is about 125 km wide at its narrowest, between the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea. The Suez Canal, a 193 km artificial waterway completed in 1869, cuts through the isthmus, providing the shortest maritime route between Europe and Asia. The isthmus is the only land connection between Africa and Eurasia, making it strategically vital for global trade. About 12% of global trade passes through the Suez Canal annually. The isthmus is composed of desert terrain with saline lakes and is crossed by multiple oil and gas pipelines.
fact: The Isthmus of Suez connects Africa and Asia, about 125 km wide · The Suez Canal crossing it was completed in 1869, a 193 km vital trade route · About 12% of global trade passes through the Suez Canal annually · The isthmus is the only land connection between Africa and Eurasia

desc: The Isthmus of Corinth is a narrow land bridge connecting the Peloponnese peninsula with the mainland of Greece, separating the Gulf of Corinth from the Saronic Gulf. It is only 6.3 km wide at its narrowest point. The Corinth Canal, completed in 1893, cuts through the isthmus, connecting the Ionian and Aegean Seas. The canal is 6.4 km long but only 21 meters wide, making it impassable for large modern ships. In ancient times, ships were hauled across the isthmus on a paved road called the Diolkos. The isthmus has been strategically important since antiquity, with the city of Corinth controlling this critical passage.
fact: The Isthmus of Corinth is only 6.3 km wide, connecting the Peloponnese to mainland Greece · The Corinth Canal (1893) cuts through at 6.4 km length but only 21 meters wide · Ancient ships were hauled across the isthmus on the paved Diolkos road · The isthmus has been strategically vital since ancient Greek times

desc: The Isthmus of Kra is the narrowest part of the Malay Peninsula in Thailand, connecting the mainland to the Malay Peninsula and Singapore. It is about 44 km wide at its narrowest point between the Andaman Sea and the Gulf of Thailand. The isthmus has been proposed for a canal project (Kra Canal) that would bypass the Strait of Malacca, though the project has never materialized. The isthmus is the traditional geographical boundary between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. The region is known for its rubber plantations, tin mining, and tourism. The proposed canal would shorten shipping routes by about 1,200 km.
fact: The Isthmus of Kra is the narrowest part of the Malay Peninsula at 44 km wide · The proposed Kra Canal would bypass the Strait of Malacca, shortening routes by 1,200 km · It marks the traditional boundary between the Indian and Pacific Oceans · The isthmus is known for rubber plantations and tin mining in Thailand
